mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mobility over the next 28 days does not show a mean increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility continues its recovery and surpasses a -40% threshold, it signifies a critical mass of people returning to offices, which will directly boost retail and recreation activities in the vicinity, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises above -40% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The decreasing trend in RESIDENTIAL mobility combined with the increasing trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests people are spending less time at home and more time on essential outings. This shift in daily routines will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decrease while GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The steady increase in TRANSIT mobility, even if slowing slightly, indicates ongoing relaxation of public transport restrictions and increased public confidence in using shared transport. This policy-driven shift will facilitate greater access to retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, provided the reopening regime continues.
failure_condition: If the government re-imposes transit restrictions, or if TRANSIT mobility declines significantly, then RETAIL_REC will not increase.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in PARKS mobility, indicating greater outdoor activity and public comfort, will translate into a short-term boost for nearby retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next week.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to increase, but RETAIL_REC mobility over the next 7 days does not show an increase.

mechanism_narrative: A combined increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, where both rise by at least 2 percentage points week-on-week, signifies a strong return to daily commutes and office work. This surge in commuter traffic will directly increase footfall in retail and recreation areas, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by >2pp AND TRANSIT increases by >2pp week-on-week
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, coupled with the gradual increase in RETAIL_REC, indicates a fundamental shift in public behavior away from staying at home and towards engaging in out-of-home activities. This behavioral momentum will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility starts to increase or RETAIL_REC mobility plateaus or declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across all mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) and the decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggest a strong underlying policy of easing restrictions and encouraging economic activity. This overarching policy environment will continue to support and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: A significant reversal in government policy, such as a re-imposition of lockdown measures, would prevent RETAIL_REC from increasing.
